description: Take the Chrysler Building apart piece by piece in 3D, and read the story of the tower: a secret spire, a skyscraper race, and seven stainless steel arches over the automobile age.

hotspots.text: Seven radiating terraced arches step the tower from the 61st floor to the 925 ft roof. Each arch is clad in Nirosta stainless steel, and each steps back from the one below.
hotspots.title: The terraced crown

hotspots.text: Radiating stainless steel fins give the crown its stylized sunburst motif, the sunrise over the automobile age. The fins catch the light differently through the day, which is why the crown seems to glow at dusk.
hotspots.title: The sunburst motif

hotspots.text: The 185 ft, 27 ton Nirosta steel spire was assembled in secret inside the crown, then raised through the roof in 90 minutes on 23 October 1929, one day before the Wall Street Crash. It beat 40 Wall Street to the title of world's tallest building.
hotspots.title: The secret spire

hotspots.text: Eight stylized American eagle heads glare from the 61st floor corners, two per corner, stainless steel like the crown above them.
hotspots.title: The eagle gargoyles

hotspots.text: The 31st floor corners carry replicas of 1929 Chrysler radiator caps, one of four. Walter Chrysler wanted his tower to advertise his cars, and the ornament obliged.
hotspots.title: Radiator cap replicas

hotspots.text: A frieze of hubcap motifs rings the 31st floor, more automobile ornament worked into the brickwork.
hotspots.title: The hubcap frieze

hotspots.text: The three story lobby ceiling carries murals by Edward Trumbull, refurbished in 1978. The lobby was listed alongside the facade in the 1978 city landmark designation.
hotspots.title: The Trumbull murals

hotspots.text: The building holds 32 elevators. Their lobby doors open off walls of Red Moroccan marble with onyx, blue marble and steel.
hotspots.title: The lobby elevators

hotspots.text: The lobby is entered from Lexington Avenue, 42nd and 43rd Streets, at 405 Lexington Avenue in Midtown Manhattan.
hotspots.title: The street entrances

intro: New York's most romantic skyscraper is 319 meters of Art Deco ambition, won with a trick: a 185 ft steel spire assembled in secret and raised through the roof in 90 minutes. This is how Walter Chrysler's tower beat 40 Wall Street to the sky.
page_title: Chrysler Building: Exploded 3D Model and History | Architectural Atlas

sections.body: Architect William Van Alen designed the tower for Walter P. Chrysler, the founder of the Chrysler Corporation, who paid for the building himself as a personal project. Its great rival was 40 Wall Street, the bank tower by H. Craig Severance, Van Alen's former partner, planned to top out at 927 ft. Van Alen answered with a trick: a 185 ft spire of Nirosta stainless steel, weighing 27 tons, assembled in secret inside the crown. On 23 October 1929, one day before the Wall Street Crash, it was raised through the roof in 90 minutes. The building opened on 27 May 1930 at 1,046 ft, the tallest in the world, and held the title for 11 months until the Empire State Building surpassed it on 1 May 1931. The secret spire remains the most famous skyscraper-race story in New York history.
sections.heading: The race for the tallest building

sections.body: The ornament is pure Chrysler. Eight stylized American eagle heads glare from the 61st floor corners; the 31st floor corners carry replicas of 1929 Chrysler radiator caps; hubcap motifs run in a frieze; car-wheel bands circle the facade. Above it all rises the crown: seven radiating terraced arches in stainless steel with a stylized sunburst motif. The shaft between is white and dark-gray brickwork laid to emphasize the horizontal window rows, all 3,862 of them, served by 32 elevators across 77 floors.
sections.heading: A tower for the automobile age

sections.body: The three story lobby is entered from Lexington Avenue, 42nd and 43rd Streets. Its walls are Red Moroccan marble with onyx, blue marble and steel, and its ceiling carries murals by Edward Trumbull, refurbished in 1978. When New York designated the building a city landmark in 1978, the lobby was listed alongside the facade.
sections.heading: The lobby

sections.body: The spire keeps getting knocked off on screen. In Godzilla (1998), US military missiles meant for Godzilla accidentally blast the spire loose and it crashes to the street, an effects shot built around a 12-foot miniature, confirmed by the effects supervisor in an American Cinematographer interview. In Armageddon (1998) the building is struck by a meteor and the spire crashes down. ArchDaily lists the tower among its film appearances in Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer, Sex and the City, Spider-Man and Deep Impact. Off screen, the building's own origin story, the secret 185 ft spire raised against Severance's 40 Wall Street, is the most famous skyscraper-race story in New York history.
sections.heading: In the cultural conversation

sections.body: The Chrysler Building became a National Historic Landmark in 1976 and a New York City landmark in 1978, covering both facade and lobby. In 2007 it ranked 9th on the AIA List of America's Favorite Architecture. The Cloud Club, a private club on the upper floors in the late 1920s to the 1970s, is part of that history too.
sections.heading: A landmark twice over

sources: Facts adapted from the Wikipedia "Chrysler Building" article (CC BY-SA) and the NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission designation report LP-0992 (12 September 1978). Cultural appearances verified against ArchDaily and American Cinematographer.

The building is completed and opened at 1,046 ft, becoming the tallest building in the world.
The Empire State Building surpasses it after 11 months as the world's tallest.
Designated a New York City landmark, covering the facade and the lobby.
Ranked 9th on the AIA List of America's Favorite Architecture.
